I have issues for EIPs up to and including spurious dragon now Something I meant to ask during the call but totally spaced on: Should we do the type audits before making the copy for homestead? (cc. <@!497280885645639691> <@!564718359304863744> <@!243183686562873344> <@!543900561460822016>) i think yes minimizes future work Okay, I'll do the bytes types today. Yeah we have to do those sooner than later. But I'll continue to work in parallel on the Homestead hard fork. The state root in a block is a variable length byte array, or a `Hash32`? Pretty sure it's the latter https://eth.wiki/fundamentals/specs/consensus-datastructures TL;DR: 32-bytes (hash). All hashes are full width, leading zeros are not stripped. Only QUANTITY values have their leading zeros stripped. Alright, next question. In the storage tries (global and per-account) what is the key type? Variable length byte array, or fixed length byte array? Probably a good question for <@!243183686562873344> >.> 32-bytes. Necessary for the MPT trie to work. From the afformentioned doc: ``` StateRoot = patriciaTrie(keccak256(Address) => rlp(Account)).rootHash StorageRoot = patriciaTrie(keccak256(StorageSlot: UInt256) => Bytes32).rootHash ``` They are hashed to ensure good distribution across the space, and all 32 bytes are used, even if the first byte is 0 that is still used. This gets kind of subtle. The State consists of a mapping `Address => Account` and a mapping `(Address, Bytes32) => U256`. But to calculate the root of a state you have to do the following process: 1. Hash all the the addresses and storage keys. 2. For each address calculate the storage root by putting all of storage slot into a MPT. 3. Put all the accounts (with their storage roots) into a MPT. 4. The root of that MPT is the state root. The conceptual point is that when Verkle tries are implemented the process for calculating a state root will change, but the state will still be a pair of mappings. So for the API for `Trie` needs to support `Address => Account` and `Bytes32 => U256`? It has to support `Uint`, `Address` and `Bytes32` as keys and `Account`, `Transaction`, `Receipt` and `U256` as values. It is `address => account_tuple` and `uint256_slot => bytes32_data` Is there a distinction between `Bytes32` and `U256`? The EVM doesn't draw one. For the sake of Ethereum wire encoding yes. Not sure if it applies here, but I think it is good to be explicit that all 32 bytes are returned, even if some are 0. The data type of each piece of data stored in a slot is opaque, it is just 32-bytes of *something*. We also have to support `Bytes32` as trie values for the `TrieTests` in the test suite. I think I'm definitely missing the point of `get_storage_root` 😐

StateRoot = patriciaTrie(keccak256(Address) => rlp(Account)).rootHash
